questions.question:
Which of the following is a non-reducing carbohydrate:-
(a)         
 
(b) 

(c) 

(d)
questions.explanation:
Problem Statement: The question asks which of the given sugar molecules is a non-reducing sugar. Non-reducing sugars do not have a free aldehyde or ketone group and therefore do not react in typical reduction tests.
Underlying Concept: Sugars can be classified as reducing or non-reducing based on the presence of a free aldehyde or ketone group. Reducing sugars have a free anomeric carbon capable of open-chain form, allowing them to reduce mild oxidizing agents. Non-reducing sugars do not have this free reactive group, often due to glycosidic linkage involving the anomeric carbons of both monosaccharide units.
Tips and Tricks: Remember that sucrose is a common example of a non-reducing sugar because its glycosidic bond links the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose, preventing free aldehyde or ketone groups.
Common Mistakes: Mistaking all disaccharides as reducing sugars. Some disaccharides like sucrose are non-reducing because of their linkage.
Why Other Options Are Incorrect?: Option (a) and (d) are reducing sugars because they have free anomeric carbons available. For example, maltose (a) and lactose (d) have a free aldehyde group in one monosaccharide unit allowing reduction.
